text: Producer/consumer orientation mismatch with mkxyz_shoal_inlet_Uchannel.f: this script maps loaded rows to y and columns to x at L13-L18, but that generator writes dep_shoal_inlet.txt with outer i rows and inner j columns. The plot at L37 therefore swaps the generated physical axes and also discards its centered/shifted coordinates.

Producer/consumer orientation mismatch with the preceding bathymetry generator: this file assumes matrix rows are y and columns are x at L3-L7. mkxyz_shoal_inlet_Uchannel.f writes dep_shoal_inlet.txt with outer i records and inner j values (its L145-L149), so loading yields rows=i and columns=j. Consequently this script maps the generator's x index onto y and its y index onto x at L6-L7/L19, transposing the physical axes without transposing dep.

Range defect across L21, L76-L87, and L97: for 0<y<100 the slope branch at L77 produces negative dep. Outside abs(x)<=150 the channel branch at L80-L83 does not replace it, and the basin branch begins only at y>=100 at L85. The later min(dep,h) at L97 preserves the negative value. depmin=0.002 at L7 is never applied, so a substantial grid region is emitted with negative depth.
Dry cells are set to NaN before `curl` (L38-L45), so MATLAB's finite differences can propagate NaNs into wet cells adjacent to the mask boundary; the source applies no one-sided boundary treatment.

Eta is masked to NaN before mirroring (L49,L53-L54), then rowwise `max`/`min` are called without `omitnan` at L97-L98. Any dry/masked cell in a row can make that row's extrema NaN rather than the wet-cell envelope, so the final red curves may disappear across rows containing shoreline masks.

`dep` is created once before the loop at L13 and then destructively masked at L42. The active one-frame range hides the effect, but any restored multi-frame range would retain NaNs from every earlier mask and prevent re-wetted cells from returning in the depth panel.
